summary:
Second probe execution recorded and the admission scoping fixed; no defect claim, and the question stays paused until a mode-scoped run is judged (valid:true).

What the receipt showed (1ac934864b0f42fd9bb658662fd71274, completed/exit 0): the identity problem was solved — probe_node_start events at indices 1-3 carry the node field and both comparisons matched their admittances — but both comparisons still came back unknown for a different wiring reason: one admission alias admitted all three nodes, and the controller then required every admitted node to produce a complete applicable result ('Admitted operation has no complete applicable result observation' for the nodes that cannot emit recovered_node_probe_end, and vice versa). The operands are consistent with the previous run: indices 7 and 9 (leader and untouched follower) show install_signature_seen false with applied_at_end equal to max_applied_seen, observed_applied_decrease false and decrease_count 0; index 8 (recovered node, rounds at indices 4-6 advancing applied 27 → 112 → 197) shows install_signature_seen true with install_signature_ticks 1214, snapshot index 257 above its log store last index 197, and again applied_at_end 257 equal to max_applied_seen with no decrease. So the node that went through the install path never reported an applied index below its maximum, which is what a rewinding install would have produced — but I did not claim holds, because the controller's comparisons were unknown and the negative reading rests on operands plus the source-side clamp analysis, not on a verdict. That account is recorded as unresolved with its limits, including that neither run constructs a leader snapshot index below a follower's applied index.

Successor requested with previous_id f96d0cb449034230970d0365462d8585-experiment and a documented revision reason: the harness now emits an explicit mode event per node — recovery_mode_entered when the install signature first appears (carrying node and the applied/snapshot/log indices at entry), steady_mode_confirmed for nodes that finish without it — and each comparison admits on its own mode alias, so admitted operations and result events cover the same node set. Producers, configuration, rounds, command counts, polling density and result event names are unchanged; the local run of the fixed harness emitted exactly one recovery_mode_entered and two steady_mode_confirmed events with matching per-node end events.
